key: Sage of the Stolen Flame fable
0.comment: Kukulkan: Hanan Pacha and the Phlogiston Fable
0.content: Natlanese tradition says the Sage and his foolish companion Chaac raised the floating land of Hanan Pacha so that curious people would come and learn Phlogiston. The records are explicitly a fable that historians dismiss; in that tale the Sage is human, steals the Pyrophosphorite from a vain winged dragon by trickery, and leaves after the people are made drunk by sweet water the Lord of the Night offered. The legend is that Phlogiston was scattered across Natlan, and the Sage set out on a "road home" that might mean he will return. Chikya believes the Sage was human, but the Upper Sanctum is shown to be Kukulkan's work.

1.content: A council record in the Chamber of Deliberation shows an impeachment inquiry into Regent Kukulkan convened on the Second Lord's initiative; the argument is erased, and the vote shows nine lords in favour and four abstaining. Shadows replayed in the chamber (Once, the Sacred Seat of Judgment, 5.5) call him the "Silver Prince", accuse him of giving humans Phlogiston and of letting an escaped test subject from his laboratory reach the human federation. In another session the Eleventh Lord sneers that the Fourth Lord shares the Regent's "facile obsession with technology". The Secret Source Servant calling itself Awanyu says the denunciations were about seizing his authority, not genuine belief, and that when Xiuhcoatl appeared in the flesh the lords withdrew their words and the trial dissolved into farce.

2.comment: Kukulkan: Huitzilopochtli and the Golden Entreaties
2.content: Huitzilopochtli, the Natlan Phlogistonization Array, would transform Natlan into Phlogiston and annihilate the Abyss by mutual annihilation, at the cost of all existing life. Two Golden Entreaties made from Xiuhcoatl's control-hub eye activate it after three confirmations. Kukulkan swore with Xbalanque never to activate it, then plotted to do so himself, and after Little One cancelled the activation he faded away.

key: Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash
3.comment: Kukulkan: Och-Kan and the Fell Dragon
3.content: Och-Kan was Kukulkan's half-dragon son and the king of Ochkanatlan. Kukulkan twisted his body into the fell dragon in the ruins and used the Jade of Return legend to draw people to Tonatiuh. Och-Kan later lamented that his spirit and body had been used by "that person" for such crimes.
